How do you know which moon is which?

Historically astronomers figured out which is which by tracking their movements to see which order they are in. Today there's plenty of tools online that guide you, but the vast majority of amateur astronomers use planetarium software called "Stellarium". Stellarium shows you how the sky appear from whichever location you punch in, where everything is in the sky and at what times. You can zoom in on Jupiter with this and it will show labelled moons. If you took photos the night before you can just rewind the software to that given time and it should match up with your photos.
